title: NAFEMS LE10 three-dimensional thick elliptical plate
purpose: Verify AgentFEM's canonical three-dimensional static-solid path against a public bending-dominated continuum benchmark with curved geometry, quadratic displacement interpolation, mixed component constraints, surface pressure, stress recovery, force balance, and work balance.
physics: three-dimensional small-strain isotropic linear elasticity under transverse pressure

source.title: LE10 Thick Plate Pressure
source.reference: The Standard NAFEMS Benchmarks, Test LE10; public target sigma_yy(D) = -5.38 MPa

execution.evidence: A curved quadratic mapped-hexahedron model compares the recovered top-surface sigma_yy at D=(2,0,0.6) with the published -5.38 MPa target while independently checking algebraic force balance, strain-energy balance, and default unsmoothed stress-field semantics.

observables: recovered top-surface sigma_yy at point D
point-D displacement against an independent public LE10 implementation
relative error against the NAFEMS -5.38 MPa target
integrated pressure resultant against the analytical quarter-ellipse area
global reaction plus applied pressure resultant
strain energy and external work balance
default DG0 cell-average stress processing metadata
acceptance: The recovered sigma_yy(D) differs from the NAFEMS target by less than 5%.
The versioned 4 x 12 x 2 curved quadratic mesh remains within 1% of the published stress target.
The point-D displacement vector remains within 3% of the independent public Fino/FeenoX result.
Relative force and energy balance errors remain below 1e-9.
The integrated loaded-area error remains below 5e-5.
The benchmark-only nodal recovery remains explicit and does not silently replace AgentFEM's traceable DG0 cell-average stress output.
limitations: The NAFEMS comparison quantity depends on a stated stress-recovery convention; raw integration-point, cell-average, nodally extrapolated, and globally projected stresses are not interchangeable.
This benchmark verifies continuum Lagrange solid mechanics, not shells, contact, plasticity, or nearly incompressible mixed formulations.
The public reference target is a numerical benchmark value rather than a closed-form solution.
